reasoning:
I'm weighing whether ordering pending_cubes by actual pick sequence breaks predictability since the policy can't know that order ahead of time, and considering instead keeping listed-area order but changing removal to match the grasped cube — which raises the question of which cube the subgoal rule should target when multiple are pending.

I'm settling on the report's approach: the annotator orders by actual pick sequence, the policy writes the list in listed order at the button-press step (accepting a mismatch there as residual uncertainty), and in later steps the policy follows the front of the carried-in list, which matches the recorded pick since it inherits the annotated ordering. This confines the mismatch to just the button-press step, which is an improvement. Now I need to write out the actual edits — the pending_cubes annotator prompt, the policy memory removal clause, and subgoal rules 3 through 5.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of pending_cubes, using the current position of the cube seen there in the scene (cube positions wobble; use the cube visible nearest the stored point).
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: choose B, pick up the highlighted cube, pointing at the FIRST entry of the pending_cubes list carried in (after removing any cube already picked up on this step; on the button-press step itself, the first entry of the list just written), using the current position of the cube seen there in the scene (cube positions wobble; use the cube visible nearest the stored point). The list is consumed from its front; an entry leaves the list by matching the cube that was grasped, never by its place in the list.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: the task is finished; choose B pointing at the cube nearest the gripper is not needed—instead repeat C (place) as a harmless no-op.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: the task is finished; choose C (place) as a harmless no-op.

policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_from: else if any cube position is remembered in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.
policy_prompt_for_subgoal.modify_to: else if any cube position is remembered in the carried-in pending_cubes choose B at its first entry; else choose A.

edits.modify_from: write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, in the order the areas are listed. Otherwise copy the list carried in, but remove the first entry of the list if the execution steps shown at this step show a cube held in the gripper (a pick-up happened). Keep the list unchanged on a step that only shows a placing (gripper opens, cube left on table). e.g. [[89, 146], [63, 150]]
edits.modify_to: write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube nearest that area, in the order the areas are listed. Otherwise copy the list carried in, keeping its order; if the execution steps shown at this step show a cube newly marked 'is held in the gripper' (the gripper descended to ~0.02 height and the fingers closed to ~46%), remove the one entry whose [y, x] is nearest the table position that cube had in the execution step just before it was lifted, whatever its place in the list, and keep every other entry in its order. Keep the list unchanged on a step that only shows a placing (fingers reopen to 100%, cube left on table). e.g. [[118, 147], [70, 152]]

edits.modify_from: write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube whose position is nearest that area, in the order the highlighted areas are listed in the observation. edits.modify_to: write one entry per highlighted area: the [y, x] of the cube whose position is nearest that area. Order the entries in the sequence the episode actually picks those cubes up, as read from the later pick-up steps, so the cube picked up next is always the first entry. At each later step whose execution steps show a cube newly marked 'is held in the gripper', remove the entry nearest the table position that cube had in the execution step just before it was lifted, keeping the remaining entries in their order; the list is unchanged at a place step. e.g. [[118, 147], [70, 152]]

revision.refused: The per-step proposals of a geometric selection rule (farthest cube, largest y, last-listed area, consuming the list from the end) stay out, as the report itself recommends: none reproduces the recorded pick order across the minibatch, and a heuristic that fails as often as it works would be one more exception each round. The pick order is therefore carried by the annotated list, which the policy follows from the front at every step after the button press. The one residual mismatch, that at the button-press step the policy writes the list in listed-area order without knowing the true pick order, is accepted rather than hidden behind a heuristic.
